intervention_dose: olaparib 300 mg PO twice daily for up to 2 years
indication: newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer with a BRCA mutation, in response after platinum-based chemotherapy
population_detail: germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutation required; FIGO stage III-IV; complete or partial response to first-line platinum. Excludes BRCA-wild-type tumours, which is the gap for this germline-wild-type, somatic-BRCA-pending patient.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 56.0 mo olaparib vs 13.8 mo placebo (5-year follow-up)

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: 7-year OS update (DiSilvestro JCO 2023); 67% vs 46.5% alive at 7y; median OS not reached vs 75.2 mo

safety_summary: Most common grade 3+ AEs were anemia (22%) and neutropenia (8%). Discontinuation for AEs 11.5% vs 2.3% placebo. AML in 1.2%; no new safety signals over long follow-up.

toxicities.notes: all reported AML cases fatal; long-term myeloid risk relevant to her marrow-toxicity veto

notes: PFS HR from the 2018 primary analysis; median PFS, OS HR and toxicity drawn from the 5-year (Banerjee 2021) and 7-year (DiSilvestro JCO 2023) follow-ups via secondary sources. Eligibility hinges on the pending somatic-BRCA call, since germline BRCA is wild-type.

intervention_dose: niraparib 200-300 mg PO once daily (individualized starting dose by weight and platelet count), up to 3 years
indication: newly-diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer at high risk of recurrence, in response after platinum-based chemotherapy
population_detail: all-comers regardless of BRCA or HRD status; HRD-positive subgroup pre-specified. Stage III with residual disease or any stage IV. Benefit larger in HRD-positive but present across the ITT, so this option does not strictly require the pending tumor HRD result.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 13.8 mo niraparib vs 8.2 mo placebo (ITT); HRD-positive 21.9 vs 10.4 mo

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: magnitude refined by the pending genomic-instability score

safety_summary: Grade 3+ hematologic AEs dominate: anemia 31%, thrombocytopenia 28.7%, neutropenia 12.8% in the primary analysis. Cytopenias engage her myelosuppression veto; individualized starting dose substantially lowers grade 3+ rates.

toxicities.notes: fixed 300 mg starting dose, primary analysis
drops to ~21.9% with individualized starting dose

notes: Only PARP option active across the ITT, so it does not gate on the pending HRD assay, though benefit is larger if HRD-positive. Cytopenia rates from the primary NEJM analysis; the 3.5-year update (Eur J Cancer 2023) reports higher cumulative grade 3+ thrombocytopenia (39.7%) but lower rates with the individualized starting dose.

intervention_dose: olaparib 300 mg PO twice daily up to 2 years + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w to 15 months total
indication: newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer in response after first-line platinum plus bevacizumab
population_detail: all on bevacizumab; benefit concentrated in HRD-positive tumours (with or without BRCA mutation). She is already on bevacizumab, so this is the closest design match, but the olaparib add-on only pays off if the pending HRD score is positive.
design: double-blind randomized placebo-controlled phase 3, all patients on bevacizumab (PAOLA-1/ENGOT-ov25)
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 22.1 mo vs 16.6 mo (ITT); HRD-positive 37.2 vs 17.7 mo

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: the subgroup the pending HRD assay would place her in

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.notes: 5-year OS rate (final OS, Ann Oncol 2023); ITT OS not significantly improved

safety_summary: Grade 3-4 AEs of interest: hypertension 19%, anemia 17% (vs <1% on bev alone), lymphopenia 7%, neutropenia 6%, fatigue/asthenia 5%. Adding a PARP inhibitor to ongoing bevacizumab compounds her bleeding/VTE caution.

toxicities.notes: bevacizumab class effect; relevant given her thrombotic/bleeding caution

notes: Closest design match because every patient is on bevacizumab, which she already receives; the olaparib add-on benefit is HRD-gated. Final OS (Ray-Coquard, Ann Oncol 2023) shows a 5-year OS gain in HRD-positive tumours but no significant ITT OS benefit.

intervention_dose: rucaparib 600 mg PO twice daily for up to 2 years
indication: newly-diagnosed advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (stage III-IV) in response after first-line platinum
population_detail: HRD-stratified; benefit in both the HRD-positive subgroup and the ITT. Germline-BRCA-wild-type status leaves her HRD placement dependent on the pending tumor assay.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 20.2 mo vs 9.2 mo (ITT); HRD-positive 28.7 vs 11.3 mo
safety_summary: Grade 3+ AEs: anemia 28.7% (vs 0% placebo), neutropenia 14.6%, ALT/AST increase 10.6%. Anemia and transaminitis are the dominant high-grade signals; cytopenias engage her myelosuppression veto.
notes: Tests rucaparib in her exact stage III-IV first-line maintenance setting with HRD stratification. Approved off-label for 1L maintenance in some settings; her HRD-subgroup placement waits on the pending tumor assay.

intervention_dose: bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w with carboplatin/paclitaxel then maintenance to ~15 months
indication: newly-diagnosed advanced epithelial ovarian / fallopian-tube / primary-peritoneal cancer (stage III incompletely resected or stage IV)
population_detail: all-comers; the PFS benefit came only from the bevacizumab-throughout (concurrent + maintenance) arm, matching her current regimen. This is the direct evidence base for the anti-angiogenic axis she is already on.

outcomes.name: PFS
outcomes.notes: median PFS gain ~3.8 mo, maintenance arm only

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: no significant OS benefit in the ITT on final analysis (JCO 2019)

safety_summary: Grade 2+ hypertension ~22.9% with bevacizumab; no significant excess of GI perforation or fistula vs control. Bleeding and thrombotic events are the relevant cautions given her VTE history and prior IVC filter.

toxicities.notes: no significant difference vs control arms in GOG-218

notes: Establishes the bevacizumab maintenance regimen she is already receiving in her exact indication and 1L setting. PFS gain came only from the maintenance arm; final analysis (Tewari JCO 2019) showed no ITT OS benefit.

intervention_dose: bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg IV q3w with carboplatin/paclitaxel then maintenance to 12 months
indication: newly-diagnosed ovarian cancer including high-risk stage IIIc/IV
population_detail: all-comers; largest benefit in the high-risk subgroup (stage IV or stage III with >1 cm residual disease), which overlaps her presentation before R0 resection.
median_dor_or_pfs: high-risk subgroup OS 39.3 vs 34.5 mo (4.8 mo gain)

safety_summary: Bevacizumab class effects: hypertension and bleeding/thrombotic events. Given her high-VTE history and prior IVC filter, bleeding and thrombosis are the cautions, though that risk is already accepted in her current plan.

notes: Open-label, so RoB above SOLO1/PAOLA-1. Reinforces bevacizumab maintenance in her 1L setting with the largest gain in the high-risk subgroup she matched pre-resection. OS update (Oza Lancet Oncol 2015) confined the survival gain to that subgroup.

indication: estrogen-receptor-positive high-grade serous ovarian cancer, maintenance after first-line therapy
population_detail: ER-positive high-grade serous histology, the patient's exact biology. Low-burden oral therapy fitting her age band and stated preference; PR-negativity tempers expected magnitude.
safety_summary: Aromatase inhibitors are low-toxicity; class effects are hot flushes, arthralgia and fatigue. No high-grade hematologic or neuropathic toxicity, which fits her vetoes. Per-term AE breakdown not extractable from the cohort report.
notes: Non-randomized cohort, so a weaker tier than the PARP and bevacizumab RCTs, but it targets her exact ER-positive high-grade serous biology with low-burden oral therapy. Source reports the recurrence-free signal without a structured per-term toxicity table; AE data not separable from this abstract/cohort report, so toxicities[] left empty per the class-effect summary.

indication: ER and/or PR-positive recurrent/metastatic granulosa-cell / sex-cord stromal ovarian tumours
population_detail: ER and/or PR-positive granulosa-cell / sex-cord stromal tumours, not high-grade serous. Included as aromatase-inhibitor mechanism precedent in ER-positive ovarian disease, not an enrolling match for her histology.

outcomes.name: DCR
outcomes.notes: clinical benefit rate at 12 weeks (1 PR + 76.3% SD); evaluable n=38

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: objective response rate, lower than retrospective-series pooled estimates

safety_summary: Well tolerated; main AEs grade 1 fatigue, hot flushes and arthralgia. Grade 3 arthralgia in 2 patients (3.7%); only 2 patients stopped for treatment-related AEs. No marrow or neuropathic toxicity that engages her vetoes.
notes: Mechanism precedent for aromatase inhibition in ER-positive ovarian disease, but in granulosa-cell/sex-cord stromal histology, not her high-grade serous tumour. High stable-disease rate supports endocrine therapy as a low-toxicity holding option, not a cytoreductive one. Safety denominator (54) is the full PARAGON anastrozole cohort.

population_detail: newly-diagnosed advanced epithelial ovarian cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, the patient's on-study setting. Pre-specified benefit in the BRCAm/HRD and PARP-maintenance subgroups links the IL-12 axis to her HRD question.

safety_summary: Intraperitoneal IL-12 immunogene therapy has been manageable in prior GEN-1 studies; characteristic effects are infusion-related and abdominal symptoms on the IP route. Topline phase 2; full per-term safety table not in the press/abstract material.
notes: Randomized phase I/II underpinning her on-study GEN-1/IMNN-001 program in her exact neoadjuvant stage III/IV setting. Efficacy from SITC 2024 topline and the 2025 ASCO survival update (abstract 5516); no peer-reviewed primary paper or PMID yet, and no structured per-term AE table in the public topline material, so toxicities[] left empty pending full publication.
